subject: Clarify: where request data is executed, transit hops, and deletion ownership
messages:
From: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@datapark.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick Q on where my requests get executed / cross-border transfers

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked the latency and the dev experience; before we move to a technical POC our security and privacy team needs a concise answer to two tight questions: where does request data land and get processed (we are an EU company and want EU-only execution), and do you ever transfer request content across borders via subprocessors or for monitoring/logging?

Can you confirm:
- Which regions might see our request data when we use the Hosted API (default) vs Dedicated?
- Are there any subprocessors that could route data outside the EU even transiently?
- What is your timeline/process for full deletion of request content if we need to trigger erasure?

Appreciate a short, technical response we can share internally.

Best,
Emma
Security Lead, DataPark
[Attachment: datapark-scan-reqs.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@datapark.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where my requests get executed / cross-border transfers

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear list — answering inline with the operational details you can share with your security team. Short version up front: yes, we can provide EU-only execution for Hosted via an EU tenancy; Dedicated and Private give you full control and no data leaves customer-controlled regions unless you enable cross-region backups or integrations.

Details:
- Hosted API (default): requests are routed to capacity based on availability and latency. By default accounts are US-hosted; for EU-only customers we offer an EU tenancy option that pins all inference execution and ephemeral storage to EU regions (Frankfurt and Amsterdam clusters).
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools that we provision in the region(s) you choose; we do not route inference requests outside the contracted regions.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): all execution occurs inside your network; Redwood control plane interactions are per the deployment contract.

Subprocessors and transient hops:
- Core cloud providers we use as subprocessors: AWS (eu-central-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west1), and Azure (northeurope) depending on customer tenancy. These are listed in the attached redwood-subprocessors-v1.pdf.
- Transient telemetry/monitoring: telemetry and metrics are aggregated and anonymized; request payloads are not stored in monitoring backends. Where we have to capture traces for debugging, that data is redacted and retained per our incident-handling policy; we can restrict support-level access via an SOC-approved plan for Enterprise customers.
- Cross-border transfers: we do not proactively move customer request content outside the customer region for Hosted EU-tenancy or Dedicated deployments. In mixed or default-hosted configurations, some control-plane metadata (billing, usage aggregates) may be replicated to US or other Redwood analytics zones — not the raw request content.

Deletion and erasure process:
- Ephemeral request layer (inference request buffers, KV cache): typically never persisted beyond the serving window (seconds to minutes) except when you enable logging/retention.
- Request logging / audit trails: by default, we retain request-level logs and minimal payload traces for 30 days to support troubleshooting and abuse detection.
- Customer-triggered erasure: for Hosted EU-tenancy and Dedicated customers we accept verified erasure requests under the DPA and execute a coordinated wipe across storage buckets and any caches within 72 hours, followed by a confirmation report.
- Private deployments: deletion is customer-managed; Redwood provides the erase scripts and verification artifacts as part of the engagement.

I attached our current subprocessors list and a short residency FAQ that I think will cover the bulk of internal questions. If your team needs SCCs or standard DPA text we can share the latest templates and SOC2 scope.

Want to loop in Karthik from our security team to detail the audit/logging and erasure verification steps? He can provide the timelines and audit evidence formats.

Thanks,
Sofia
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-subprocessors-v1.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]
[Attachment: residency-faq-2026.pdf (PDF, 68KB)]

From: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@datapark.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Park <oliver.park@datapark.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where my requests get executed / cross-border transfers

Thanks Sofia — helpful. Two follow-ups from our privacy team:
1) For the 30-day request logs, what fields are included (full prompt, model output, token counts, request id)? We need to know if prompts are retained verbatim.
2) For the 72-hour erasure process: does that include any backups / snapshot copies held by cloud providers (e.g., snapshots of block storage) or only Redwood-managed object stores?

Putting Karthik in copy to confirm the erasure verification artifact we would expect (audit log + hash of deleted blobs or a signed confirmation).

Oliver (sec ops) might push for a stricter default retention for the POC (7 days) — is that configurable for trials?

Best,
Emma

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Nguyen <emma.nguyen@datapark.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on where my requests get executed / cross-border transfers

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the follow-ups. Ill be concrete so you can hand this to your privacy reviewer.

1) What the 30-day logs contain: by default Hosted "request logs" contain metadata (request id, timestamp, model variant, token counts, latency) and a truncated request/response sample used for debugging (first 1,000 chars of prompt + model reply up to 2,000 chars) unless you opt-out of logging. We can turn prompt capture off for the POC so only metadata is retained. For Dedicated customers we offer a log-only mode that records token counts and request IDs without capturing prompt text.

2) Snapshots/backups: our standard erasure flow wipes Redwood-managed object stores, caches, and search indices. For cloud provider-level snapshots (EBS/GCE persistent disks) we coordinate with the provider and make sure any customer-mounted volumes used for persistence are also scrubbed per the provider's snapshot lifecycle; however, for Hosted EU-tenancy we avoid persistent provider-level snapshots of raw request content. If your procurement requires explicit provider snapshot deletion assurances we can include that in the contract and add a short SLA item.

3) Configurable retention for POC: yes — for trials we can set retention to 7 days and disable prompt capture. That is a pre-POC config change (no code change required) and Marissa (cc) will apply it to the POC tenancy and confirm via a signed configuration change note.

4) Erasure verification artifact: we provide a two-part artifact: (a) a signed audit log entry that records the erasure operation and the resource identifiers, and (b) a reconciliation CSV listing the deleted object keys and a SHA256 hash per object. For EU-tenancy and Dedicated customers we can provide the signed artifact within 5 business days of completion.

If youd like, Marissa can schedule a short call to walk through the verification artifact format and provide the DPA/SCCs.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Trust & Security (engagement)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: erasure-artifact-sample.txt (TXT, 3KB)]
